title: Motor6D
summary: A joint that connects two parts with a controllable transform — the joint type used in character rigs and animations. C0/C1 define rest poses; animating Transform (or via Animations) rotates limbs.

properties.name: Part0 / Part1
properties.description: The two joined parts (Part0 is the 'parent' side in a rig).

properties.name: C0 / C1
properties.description: The joint's anchor CFrames relative to Part0 and Part1. They define how the parts sit at rest.

properties.name: Transform
properties.description: The current joint rotation/offset between the C0 and C1 anchors — animations drive this.

properties.name: DesiredAngle / MaxVelocity / CurrentAngle
properties.description: Legacy motor controls (mostly superseded by Animations).

details.heading: The rig invariant
details.body: Part1.CFrame ≈ Part0.CFrame * C0 * Transform * C1:Inverse(). Animations animate Transform; the rig pose follows.

explanation.whatItIs: A hinge-with-memory: it holds two parts together at a defined pose AND can rotate between poses. Every animated character joint is one.
explanation.whyItExists: Welds freeze; characters must bend. Motor6D gives joints a pose that animations can change.
whenToUse: Building custom rigs (robots, creatures, vehicles with moving parts)
Understanding why character limbs move (Animations write Motor6D transforms)
Manual posing: adjust Transform for procedural animation
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Part0 ──(C0)──◉──(Transform)──◉──(C1)── Part1
                joint pivot
Animations = "change Transform over time"
```
tips: R6/R15 characters are just trees of Motor6Ds — inspect one to learn
For procedural aiming, only touch the relevant joint's Transform each frame
Keep C0/C1 authored at bind pose; don't animate them
commonMistakes: Setting C0/C1 at runtime and breaking the rest pose
Mixing animation playback with manual Transform writes (they fight)
Expecting Motor6D to act like a physics hinge (it's kinematic)

examples.title: Simple two-part joint
examples.code:
local base = workspace.ArmBase
local arm = workspace.ArmPart

local joint = Instance.new("Motor6D")
joint.Part0 = base
joint.Part1 = arm
-- Anchor the joint at the top of the base / bottom of the arm:
joint.C0 = CFrame.new(0, base.Size.Y / 2, 0)
joint.C1 = CFrame.new(0, -arm.Size.Y / 2, 0)
joint.Parent = base

-- Later: swing the arm
joint.Transform = CFrame.Angles(math.rad(45), 0, 0)
